findings.explanation: The detection is sourced from kube-state-metrics, kube-scheduler metrics and kube:events FailedScheduling, not the Performance data model (which only feeds a cosmetic appendcols column); 'macro involvedObject.kind' is a field, not a macro, and the alert gate in the SPL is pending_soak_min >= 8, not 25.
findings.quote: sourced from datamodel `Performance`. Threshold bundle: `mv` > 0, `pend` > 0, `mv` > 0, or `pending_soak_min` >= 25
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual signal: Pods Pending for at least 8 minutes with PodScheduled=false and/or FailedScheduling events, classified by scheduler message (insufficient CPU/memory, taints, affinity, topology spread, GPU), with severity rising at 15, 20 and 25 minutes.

findings.explanation: Pod scheduling failures are Kubernetes object state and events; neither Application_State (service/process inventory) nor Performance represents them, and the detection does not depend on either model.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the CIM mapping (state that the UC runs on raw kube-state-metrics and kube:events) and drop the matching dataModelAcceleration advice.

findings.explanation: Twenty 'Platform scheduling note N' paragraphs repeat the same template sentence with one topic swapped in, followed by generic 'X alignment' paragraphs and a generator closing checklist; they add length without implementation guidance.
findings.quote: Platform scheduling note 1: watch for topology spread on single-zone lab clusters; extend coalesce ladders after migrations and document compensating kubectl procedures when metrics are unavailable.
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse the twenty notes into a short list of the few that change behaviour (priority/preemption, GPU device plugins, maxPods/ENI limits, init-container request sums), and delete the alignment paragraphs and the closing checklist.

findings.explanation: The SPL never filters or escalates on workload_tier, so gold and sandbox namespaces page identically; the critical_namespaces.csv join is on namespace only, so identically named namespaces in different clusters share a tier.
findings.quote: page gold namespaces when pending_soak_min crosses eight minutes with FailedScheduling text or elevated scheduler_unschedulable_pods
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe tier-based routing as an alert-action step the operator adds (for example where workload_tier="gold" for paging) or note that the base search does not apply it; key the lookup on cluster plus namespace.

findings.explanation: Marked verified by a generic handle although the SPL fails to parse.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft/community until the search runs on real data.

findings.explanation: The repository guide names only the splunk-otel-collector Helm chart; a 'Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes' documentation page may not exist or may not apply. The EKS best-practices link has also moved to docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the add-on page resolves and is relevant, otherwise link the Helm chart repository; update the EKS best-practices URL.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Every multisearch arm contains stats (and the first also sort and streamstats); multisearch subsearches must be purely streaming, so the search errors out.

`involvedObject.name` and `involvedObject.kind` are wrapped in backticks, which SPL treats as macro invocations, so the search fails with an unknown-macro error; dotted field names in eval need single quotes ('involvedObject.name').

pending_soak_min is now() minus the first Pending bucket in the 45-minute window, with no check that the Pod is still Pending, so a Pod that scheduled 30 minutes ago keeps scoring as a long soak. Use the last Pending bucket time and require it to be recent.

sort - severity orders tier strings lexicographically (medium, low, high, critical), putting medium rows first; latest() on scheduler_pending_pods picks an arbitrary queue label (active/backoff/unschedulable/gated) instead of the unschedulable queue.

The appendcols tstats uses nodename=Performance.Memory and Performance.mem_used_percent, which are not valid CIM paths (All_Performance.Memory), and appendcols attaches the value to the first result row only.

nodename=Performance.CPU, Performance.cpu_load_percent and Performance.host are not valid CIM Performance paths (root is All_Performance; host is All_Performance.dest), and host CPU joined to Application_State does not express a scheduling-failure detection.
The array contains the free-text value 'N/A (operational reliability monitoring)' instead of being empty.

summary: The detection design (kube-state-metrics Pending soak, PodScheduled=false, FailedScheduling message taxonomy, scheduler gauges) and the troubleshooting cases are genuinely useful, but the SPL cannot run (non-streaming commands inside multisearch, field names wrapped in macro backticks), soak timing ignores whether the Pod is still Pending, the CIM mapping and cimSpl are invalid, and Step 1 is padded with twenty near-identical template notes.
